High-frequency linear (7–15 MHz) grayscale and color Doppler sonography of the anterior abdominal wall was performed over the region of clinical concern at rest and during Valsalva maneuvers in supine and standing positions.
Location: Linea alba immediately surrounding the umbilicus.

Fascial Layer & Defect: High-frequency evaluation of the linea alba immediately surrounding the umbilicus demonstrates an intact, continuous hyperechoic fascial layer. No focal fascial defect or abnormal protrusion of preperitoneal fat or bowel is identified at rest or during Valsalva maneuvers in supine and upright positions.
Hernia Sac & Contents: No hernia sac is present.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Normal bilateral rectus abdominis muscles without diastasis recti. Overlying subcutaneous fat is unremarkable with no focal lipoma, fluid collection, or hyperemia.
Normal targeted abdominal wall ultrasound; no sonographic evidence of a paraumbilical hernia.

subs.title: Paraumbilical Hernia (Adjacent to Umbilicus)
items: Immediately [superior / inferior / lateral] to the umbilicus, there is an eccentric linea alba fascial defect measuring [X.X] cm in width through which a paraumbilical hernia sac measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm protrudes, containing [non-reducible omental fat and viable small bowel].

subs.title: Diastasis Recti (Important Mimic — Not a True Hernia)
items: Widening and thinning of the midline linea alba is noted between the medial borders of the bilateral rectus abdominis muscles, measuring [X.X] cm in maximal inter-rectus distance (normal less than 2.0 cm), with smooth anterior bulging during head-lift/Valsalva but no discrete fascial defect or hernia sac, consistent with diastasis recti.

subs.title: Incarcerated vs. Strangulated Abdominal Wall Hernia
items: Incarcerated (Viable): The hernia contents are fixed and non-reducible upon graded transducer compression; however, the herniated [fat / bowel] maintains normal echogenicity, normal wall thickness, and preserved color Doppler vascularity without fluid in the hernia sac.

Strangulated (Emergency): The non-reducible hernia sac contains a thick-walled, aperistaltic, fluid-filled bowel loop (wall thickness [X.X] mm) with surrounding free fluid within the sac and absent intramural color Doppler flow, concerning for strangulation.

bank.title: PART 2: EXAMPLE FINDINGS FROM THE SAMPLE ABNORMAL REPORT
items: Paraumbilical Region: Immediately superior to the umbilicus (supraumbilical / paraumbilical), there is a midline fascial defect measuring 1.5 cm in transverse width through which an incarcerated paraumbilical hernia sac measuring 3.6 x 2.8 x 2.2 cm protrudes into the subcutaneous tissue. The sac contains non-reducible, lobulated omental fat and a short loop of non-dilated small bowel. No reduction occurs with probe compression. The herniated bowel loop retains normal wall thickness (2.3 mm), sluggish peristalsis, and preserved color Doppler vascularity, with no free sac fluid.
Incarcerated paraumbilical hernia (neck width 1.5 cm, sac 3.6 cm) containing non-reducible omental fat and viable small bowel, without sonographic signs of strangulation.
